record.paper_title: Some open problems on Banach spaces
record.original_question: Does the James space J admit an equivalent norm under which it has the 2-Daugavet property, meaning that every finite-rank operator T from J to J satisfies ||Id + T||^2 >= 1 + ||T||^2?

evidence.quote: Let us say that a Banach space X possesses the 2-Daugavet property if every finite rank operator T : X → X satisfies kId + Tk 2 ≥ 1 + kTk2.
Problem 1.1. Is it true that the James space J possesses the 2-Daugavet property in some equivalent norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $J$ denote the James space, that is, the Banach space of all sequences $(x_n)_{n\geq 1}$ of real numbers with $x_n \to 0$ and finite squared variation norm
$$\|x\|_J = \sup\Big\{\Big(\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}(x_{p_{k+1}}-x_{p_k})^2 + (x_{p_1}-x_{p_m})^2\Big)^{1/2} : 1\le p_1<p_2<\cdots<p_m\Big\}^{1/2}\cdot 2^{-1/2},$$
(equivalently, the standard James-space norm under which $J$ is quasi-reflexive of order one). Say that a Banach space $X$ has the 2-Daugavet property if every finite-rank operator $T: X \to X$ satisfies
$$\|\mathrm{Id} + T\|^2 \geq 1 + \|T\|^2.$$
Question: Does there exist an equivalent norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $J$ under which $J$ has the 2-Daugavet property?

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source that resolves whether the James space admits an equivalent norm with the 2-Daugavet property. No paper announcing a solution (positive or negative) was located, so the current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses geometric/diameter-two properties of James-type spaces but does not address the 2-Daugavet renorming question.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on James-space renormings does not contain a resolution of the 2-Daugavet renorming question.
